heading: 1. Introduction
text: Whitespace, comments, and harmless formatting differences should not change the resulting schema model.

heading: 1. Introduction
text: At the same time, a deterministic CDDL layer must not erase supported CDDL semantics that a consuming domain may treat as meaningful.

heading: 4. Terminology
text: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14.

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: 5. Processing Model

heading: 5. Processing Model
text:
source text
  -> parse
      parsed syntax
  -> resolve
      resolved CDDL rule graph
  -> canonicalize
      canonical CDDL schema model
  -> encode
      RFC 8949-based deterministic CBOR bytes

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The parse and resolve stages MUST follow RFC 8610 semantics for the supported subset.

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: A `cdCDDLe` implementation MAY expose parsing and resolution as part of the same tool.

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: If it does, parse or resolution errors MUST be reported before canonicalization.

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: Before canonicalization, an implementation MUST verify that the resolved CDDL rule graph uses only the constructs in Section 5.1.

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: It MUST reject any other construct rather than omit it, approximate it, or assign it an implementation-local representation.

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The canonicalization stage MUST NOT depend on:

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The canonicalization stage MUST NOT depend on: … source file byte offsets;

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The canonicalization stage MUST NOT depend on: … comments;

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The canonicalization stage MUST NOT depend on: … indentation;

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The canonicalization stage MUST NOT depend on: … source line wrapping;

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The canonicalization stage MUST NOT depend on: … non-semantic whitespace;

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The canonicalization stage MUST NOT depend on: … implementation-specific parser object identity;

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The canonicalization stage MUST NOT depend on: … host-language map iteration order.

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: The encoding stage MUST encode the canonical model as deterministic CBOR using the rules in Section 9.

heading: 5.1 Supported CDDL Construct Subset
text: 5.1 Supported CDDL Construct Subset

heading: 5.1 Supported CDDL Construct Subset
text: A consumer that requires a root rule MUST identify it separately by bound rule name or construct a domain-specific root after canonicalization.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: 6. Canonical Model Requirements

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The canonical CDDL schema model MUST be a data model, not a byte string.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST be able to represent:

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST be able to represent: … non-generic type rules and named references;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST be able to represent: … the primitive types and literal values listed in Section 5.1;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST be able to represent: … fixed-length arrays, homogeneous variable-length arrays, and finite maps;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST be able to represent: … required and optional members;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST be able to represent: … ordered type choices;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST be able to represent: … inclusive integer ranges; and

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST be able to represent: … `.size` control applications.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST preserve bound rule names.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST preserve all semantics of the supported constructs except RFC 8610 implicit root selection, which is outside the model as specified in Section 5.1.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST preserve references as references unless an explicit canonicalization rule in this specification requires expansion.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: `cdCDDLe` MUST NOT silently replace all named references with their expanded structure.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts:

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … a rule definition;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … a reference to a rule;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … a primitive type;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … a literal value;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … a map entry;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … an array member;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … a member occurrence;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … a choice alternative;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … an inclusive range;

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: The model MUST distinguish at least these concepts: … a `.size` control application.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: Every resolved rule graph within the supported subset MUST have a corresponding canonical model representation.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: A canonical model document MUST contain at least one rule.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: Every bound rule name and reference name MUST be a syntactically valid RFC 8610 CDDL identifier.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: Bound rule names MUST be unique within one canonical document and MUST NOT equal a primitive name listed in Section 5.1.

heading: 6. Canonical Model Requirements
text: Every reference MUST have been resolved successfully before canonicalization.

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: 7. Canonicalization Rules

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: `cdCDDLe` MUST remove presentation information.

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: Whitespace, comments, source indentation, and line wrapping MUST NOT affect the canonical model.

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: `cdCDDLe` MUST normalize syntactic forms that are unambiguously equivalent in CDDL.

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: `cdCDDLe` MUST NOT normalize by arbitrary structural equivalence.

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: Two named rules with the same structure MUST remain distinguishable in the canonical model because the bound names remain present.

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: An implementation MAY expose structural equivalence as a derived view, but that view MUST NOT replace the name-preserving canonical model.

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: `cdCDDLe` MUST NOT derive a universal schema identifier from canonical bytes as part of this specification.

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: Applications MAY hash canonical schema bytes for their own purposes, but the meaning of that hash belongs to the consuming application profile.

heading: 7. Canonicalization Rules
text: `cdCDDLe` MUST NOT decide that two schemas are the same merely because they accept the same set of data items.

heading: 7.1 Rule Ordering
text: 7.1 Rule Ordering

heading: 7.1 Rule Ordering
text: After parsing and resolution, top-level rules MUST be ordered by their canonical rule key before encoding.

heading: 7.1 Rule Ordering
text: Map members MUST be sorted by their text key in Unicode scalar value order.

heading: 7.2 Choice Ordering
text: 7.2 Choice Ordering

heading: 7.2 Choice Ordering
text: `cdCDDLe` MUST NOT reorder choice alternatives by structural identity, encoded bytes, diagnostic order, or implementation-specific matching behavior.

heading: 7.2 Choice Ordering
text: If an order can affect diagnostics, matching behavior, or a domain interpretation, the order should remain represented.

heading: 7.3 Reference Expansion
text: 7.3 Reference Expansion

heading: 7.3 Reference Expansion
text: `cdCDDLe` MUST NOT fully inline all references by default.

heading: 7.3 Reference Expansion
text: The resolved rule/reference relation MAY form a graph.

heading: 7.3 Reference Expansion
text: That graph MAY contain cycles if the underlying CDDL schema and resolver accept them.

heading: 7.3 Reference Expansion
text: Any diagnostic or derived expanded view that follows references recursively MUST detect cycles and mark or reject the expansion according to that derived view's own rules.

heading: 7.3 Reference Expansion
text: A derived structural-equivalence view MUST be separately identified and MUST NOT replace the name-preserving canonical model defined here.

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: 7.4 Construct Mapping

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows:

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … a type rule maps to a type-rule node containing its bound name and canonicalized body;

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … a named reference maps to a type-reference node, while a primitive keyword maps to a primitive node;

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … a non-negative integer, negative integer, Boolean, text-string, or byte-string value maps to the corresponding literal node;

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … parentheses around a supported type expression are removed;

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … an array or map maps to an array or map node whose group contains its canonicalized members;

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … a bareword or text-string literal colon key maps to a member-key node containing a text-string literal with the parsed key text;

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … an absent occurrence maps to no occurrence field, `?` maps to an occurrence with bounds zero and one, and `*` maps to an occurrence with lower bound zero and upper bound `"unbounded"`;

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … a type choice maps to one choice node containing its alternatives in resolved order;

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … an inclusive integer range maps to a range node whose inclusive fields are both `true`; and

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A canonicalizer MUST map every supported source construct as follows: … a `.size` application maps to a `.size` control-application node.

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: After parentheses are removed, canonicalization MUST recursively flatten any type choice that is an alternative of another type choice into the enclosing choice node while preserving resolved alternative order.

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A choice node MUST contain at least two alternatives.

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: Canonicalization MUST reject an inclusive integer range whose lower bound exceeds its upper bound, including a range used as a `.size` controller.

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: An inclusive range with equal bounds MUST canonicalize to its single literal value rather than a range node.

heading: 7.4 Construct Mapping
text: A `.size` range controller with equal bounds MUST canonicalize to one non-negative integer literal.

heading: 9. Deterministic CBOR Encoding
text: 9. Deterministic CBOR Encoding

heading: 9. Deterministic CBOR Encoding
text: When the canonical CDDL schema model is encoded as bytes, it MUST be encoded as deterministic CBOR.

heading: 9. Deterministic CBOR Encoding
text: The encoding MUST follow the core deterministic encoding requirements in RFC 8949 Section 4.2.1.

heading: 9. Deterministic CBOR Encoding
text: The encoding MUST use shortest-form integer encodings.

heading: 9. Deterministic CBOR Encoding
text: The encoding MUST use definite-length strings, arrays, and maps.

heading: 9. Deterministic CBOR Encoding
text: The encoding MUST NOT use indefinite-length items.

heading: 9. Deterministic CBOR Encoding
text: The encoding MUST sort map keys by bytewise lexicographic comparison of the complete deterministic CBOR encoding of each map key.

heading: 9. Deterministic CBOR Encoding
text: Sorting by key length before key byte content MUST NOT be used.

heading: 10. Decoding And Checking
text: 10. Decoding And Checking

heading: 10. Decoding And Checking
text: A `cdCDDLe` decoder MUST reject CBOR bytes that are not valid deterministic CBOR under the RFC 8949-based rules in Section 9.

heading: 10. Decoding And Checking
text: A `cdCDDLe` decoder MUST reject unknown node kinds, unknown fields, absent or invalid required fields, forbidden optional fields, duplicate map keys, an empty document rule array, an empty choice, invalid rule or reference names, duplicate bound rule names, a literal whose value does not match its literal kind, an invalid range or occurrence, an unsupported primitive or control operator, and any other violation of Section 8.

heading: 10. Decoding And Checking
text: The decoder MUST verify that top-level rules and map members occur in canonical order.

heading: 10. Decoding And Checking
text: It MUST NOT accept and silently reorder a non-canonical model.

heading: 10. Decoding And Checking
text: A `cdCDDLe` checker MUST verify that a byte string is the unique deterministic encoding of a valid canonical CDDL schema model.

text: 11. Conformance

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` canonicalizer MUST:

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` canonicalizer MUST: … accept every resolved CDDL rule graph satisfying the supported-subset and canonical-model validity rules;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` canonicalizer MUST: … reject unsupported CDDL constructs explicitly;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` canonicalizer MUST: … remove presentation information;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` canonicalizer MUST: … preserve bound rule names;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` canonicalizer MUST: … preserve named references;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` canonicalizer MUST: … preserve the supported semantics identified in Section 6;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` canonicalizer MUST: … produce the same canonical model for inputs that differ only in presentation;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` canonicalizer MUST: … produce deterministic CBOR bytes for the canonical model using Section 9.

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` encoder MUST:

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` encoder MUST: … encode only valid canonical CDDL schema models;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` encoder MUST: … use the RFC 8949-based deterministic CBOR rules required by this specification;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` encoder MUST: … produce a single byte string for a given canonical model.

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` decoder/checker MUST:

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` decoder/checker MUST: … reject non-deterministic CBOR encodings;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` decoder/checker MUST: … reject malformed canonical model objects;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` decoder/checker MUST: … reject unsupported node kinds or fields;

heading: 11. Conformance
text: A conforming `cdCDDLe` decoder/checker MUST: … expose the canonical model without assigning application-specific identity.

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: 12. Conformance Vectors

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: Machine-readable conformance vectors for this specification MUST use this structure:

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text:
cdcddle-vector = {
    "name": tstr,
    ? "input-cddl": tstr,
    ? "input-cbor-hex": tstr,
    "expect": "valid" / "invalid",
    ? "canonical-diagnostic": tstr,
    ? "canonical-cbor-hex": tstr,
    ? "error-class": tstr,
    ? "notes": tstr,
}

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: Exactly one of `input-cddl` and `input-cbor-hex` MUST be present.

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A valid normative vector MUST include `canonical-cbor-hex` containing the lowercase hexadecimal encoding of the complete deterministic-CBOR `cdCDDLe` document node.

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: It MAY also include diagnostic notation for review.

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: An invalid normative vector MUST include `error-class` and MUST NOT include `canonical-diagnostic` or `canonical-cbor-hex`.

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least:

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … presentation equivalence for whitespace, comments, numeric spelling, and string escaping;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … top-level rule-order equivalence;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … preservation of distinct bound rule names with identical structure;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … preservation of choice alternative order;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … preservation of named references rather than full inlining;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … rejection of every unsupported construct category listed in Section 5.1;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … rejection of empty documents and empty choices;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … rejection of duplicate rule names, invalid reference names, invalid literal-kind and value pairs, invalid ranges, and invalid occurrences;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … rejection of unknown node kinds and fields;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … rejection of non-canonical rule and map-member ordering;

heading: 12. Conformance Vectors
text: A conformance vector set claiming complete coverage MUST include at least: … rejection of non-deterministic CBOR encodings of the canonical model.

heading: 5. Processing Model
text: For text-string and byte-string literals, the grammar and escape rules MUST follow [RFC 9682] Section 2.

heading: 5.1 Supported CDDL Construct Subset
text: Source occurrence indicators with explicit numeric bounds MUST be rejected, even when their cardinality equals that of a supported form.

heading: 5.1 Supported CDDL Construct Subset
text: Range bounds, including those in `.size` controllers, MUST be integer literals written directly in the source.

heading: 5.1 Supported CDDL Construct Subset
text: Named references as range bounds MUST be rejected.

heading: 5.1 Supported CDDL Construct Subset
text: Integer literals and integer range bounds MUST be between -18446744073709551616 and 18446744073709551615, inclusive.

heading: 5.1 Supported CDDL Construct Subset
text: An inclusive range whose lower bound exceeds its upper bound is outside the supported subset and MUST be rejected.

heading: 10. Decoding And Checking
text: A `cdCDDLe` decoder MUST reject a choice node that has another choice node as a direct alternative.
